findings.judgment: Analytically demonstrated false quantitative theorem under the stated logarithmic definition
findings.title: Theorem 3.1 omits admissible logarithmic corrections

source_locations.label: Proof of Theorem 3.1, tube-volume O(d^q) step

findings.source_claim: If a relatively compact open Z has volume-decay order q, there is C>0 depending only on Z such that e_k(Z)>-C k^((2-q)/4) for all k.
findings.suspect_step: The liminf defining order is treated as a uniform upper bound V_d=O(d^q).
findings.method: Analytic construction and proof, not finite-sample extrapolation.
findings.parameters: A=10^-3, m=10, a_i=A log(i+m)/(i+m)^(3/5), r_i=sqrt(a_i/pi), one fixed union of disjoint radius-r_i balls placed in dyadic cubes in [0,1]^4.
all_hypotheses_checked: Open subset of standard symplectic R^4
Finite positive volume S/2, S=sum a_i^2<445 A^2
No connectedness premise in the theorem; source itself permits infinite disconnected sets
Inner boundary-layer volume has logarithmic order q=2/3
ECH ball and disjoint-union axioms apply via compact exhaustion; the finite optimization for each k attains a saturated-cost maximum
findings.decisive_result: V_d asymptotic up to constants to d^(2/3)(log(1/d))^(5/3), while -e_k >= c k^(1/3)(log k)^(5/3) for all sufficiently large k. Every finite C in the displayed theorem fails for this one fixed Z.
findings.proof_reference: Report Section 3, equations (3.2)-(3.12), including dyadic placement, tube estimates, optimizer exchange, and lower bound on active balls.
findings.alternative_reading: A uniform power-law upper bound, as explicitly assumed in Proposition 3.2, excludes this example. That is stronger than equation (2.2).
findings.impact: The exact endpoint estimate and its asserted equivalence are false. This quantitative theorem is a central input, hence Major. The dimension inequality and principal packing obstructions are not refuted.

repair.statement: Strengthen to a uniform O(d^q) hypothesis, or for each 0<epsilon<q allow k^((2-q+epsilon)/4).
repair.verified_scope: The logarithmic definition implies the weaker power bound for each epsilon; the dimension bound survives epsilon tending to zero and the strict exponent comparison in Theorem 5.2 permits sufficiently small loss.
repair.not_claimed: No claim that the exact endpoint survives; no journal-version correction claim.

findings.judgment: Actual independent exact calculation disproves symplecticity of the displayed core map
findings.title: The double-positive shear in Proposition 6.1 is not symplectic

source_locations.label: Steps 2a-2b, G and Hamiltonian vector field

findings.source_claim: The displayed composition is a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism used in the bounded symplectic realization.
findings.suspect_step: Both y and u shear terms are assigned the same positive sign.
findings.parameters: f(r)=(1+r)^(-3/2); an interior fiber patch with 0<x<1, where chi(x)=x.
all_hypotheses_checked: f is positive, smooth, decreasing and integrable on [0,infinity)
The original domain has a nonempty interior fiber patch with 0<x<1
The prescribed chi equals x on this patch
Standard form is dx wedge dy + du wedge dv
findings.method: Symbolic differential-form derivation plus executed independent rational-matrix computation.
findings.decisive_result: For Psi=(x,y+(v+1/2)chi'(x),u+chi(x),v), Psi^*omega-omega=2chi'(x) dx wedge dv. On the selected patch the pairing on (partial_x,partial_v) is 2 instead of 0.
findings.alternative_reading: Changing the global Hamiltonian convention changes both signs and does not make the displayed double-positive map symplectic.
findings.impact: The explicit core construction in Proposition 6.1 and its use in Proposition 1.3 lack a valid displayed symplectic map. Existence of a bounded realization is not disproved.

repair.statement: Negate the y-displacement while retaining the u-displacement.
repair.verified_scope: Local pullback cancellation only, verified analytically and by exact rational matrices.
repair.remaining: Image-strip bounds, wrapping, global injectivity, and boundary-dimension estimates require rechecking; no full construction repair asserted.

findings.judgment: False local identity with the required downstream conclusion independently repaired under the original assumptions
findings.title: Convex erosion followed by dilation does not recover the domain

source_locations.label: Use of linear volume decay for the convex case of Theorem 1.4

findings.source_claim: The convex domain is the radius-d tube around its inner erosion, giving V_d=N_d(Z(d))-N_0(Z(d)).
all_hypotheses_checked: Z is convex and has nonempty interior
The counterexample lies inside Z and has strict distances, so a positive-volume neighborhood witnesses failure
findings.method: Analytic distance and tube-volume calculation; executed independent exact rational distance and volume check.
findings.decisive_result: dist(x,boundary Z)=d/4<d but dist(x,Z(d))=3d/2>d. At d=1/4 actual layer volume is 15/16, whereas the claimed tube difference is 1/4+13pi/96+pi^2/512 (about 0.6947005763).
findings.alternative_reading: The strict inequalities and positive-volume discrepancy survive choices of open or closed tubes.
findings.impact: The identity is false, but the lemma's order-one conclusion and its downstream convex-domain premise hold with unchanged assumptions. This is a local Minor finding, not a refutation of Theorem 1.4.

repair.statement: Translate and choose rB subset K=closure(Z) subset RB; then (1-d/r)K subset K_d subset (1-d/R)K for 0<d<r.
repair.verified_scope: Convexity and support functions yield (vol K/R)d <= V_d <= (4 vol K/r)d, proving the exact required order-one conclusion.

problem_reviews.definitions_and_quantifiers: p.7 defines q by liminf(log V_d/log d); p.11 requires only relatively compact open Z, not connectedness, and concludes a single C for all k. Proposition 3.2 has a genuinely stronger uniform power hypothesis.
problem_reviews.admissibility: For A=10^-3,m=10,a_i=A log(i+m)/(i+m)^(3/5), a_i decreases and sum a_i^2<445A^2. Dyadic cubes of side in [2r_i,4r_i) have total fourth-volume <256 sum a_i^2/pi^2<1, so sequential grid placement in [0,1]^4 works. The one fixed union of open balls is relatively compact with volume S/2.
problem_reviews.independent_decisive_reason: Every component sphere is boundary; the inner tube is the sum of ball shells. Inverting r_i yields N(d) comparable to d^(-10/3) log(1/d)^(5/3), and both shell contributions give V_d comparable to d^(2/3) log(1/d)^(5/3); hence q=2/3. Compact subsets meet finitely many components, and the ball/disjoint-union axioms reduce each k to a maximum on the first k balls. The triangle cost saturates because an unused ball can absorb one unit of slack.
problem_reviews.optimizer_check: For an optimizer with n positive entries, D=ceil(sqrt(2k)),N=n+D, lowering d_j by 1 and activating d_j unused balls proves a_j>=d_j a_N. Thus k<=sum d_j^2<=S/a_N^2 and n is bounded below by c k^(5/6)(log k)^(5/3). Cauchy-Schwarz at saturated cost gives -e_k >=(sqrt(2)-1)sum_(i<=n)a_i, hence >=c k^(1/3)(log k)^(5/3). This contradicts every finite endpoint C, not merely a finite numerical fit.
problem_reviews.counterevidence_impact_and_repair: Strengthening to V_d=O(d^q) excludes the example. For each epsilon>0 the original liminf implies V_d<=C_epsilon d^(q-epsilon), so the weaker exponent estimate survives. The p.22 strict exponent separation and the dimension limit survive sufficiently small loss. Major applies to the false core quantitative guarantee, not to the surviving packing conclusions.

problem_reviews.definitions_and_hypotheses: The standard complex coordinates, f(0)=1, nonincreasing finite-integral f and the three-map construction are explicit on p.24. f(r)=(1+r)^(-3/2) is admissible. On an interior 0<x<1 patch chi'=1; p.25 has G=v+1/2 and X_G=partial_u.
problem_reviews.independent_decisive_reason: The exact double-positive shears on p.26 pull back dx wedge dy and du wedge dv to contributions of the same sign, giving Psi*omega-omega=2chi'(x) dx wedge dv. The original pairing (partial_x,partial_v) is 0 and the new one is 2 on the admissible patch. Changing Hamiltonian convention cannot cancel this two-positive defect.
problem_reviews.dependency_and_severity: Proposition 6.1 explicitly declares Psi a symplectic embedding in the composition F=Xi o Psi o Phi, and Step 4 uses it for the bounded symplectic realization. This is a demonstrated invalid derivation tied to the core construction. Under review-contract line52, a short repair does not lower that core error to Minor; the existence theorem itself has not been refuted.
problem_reviews.counterevidence_and_repair_boundary: Replacing y+G chi' by y-G chi' restores symplecticity. The additional constant y-translation 1+delta restores the same strip (0,infinity)x(0,2+delta), since 0<=G chi'<=1+delta. This leaves x,u,v, w-projection area and the separation of fibers with |x1-x2|>=1 unchanged; the inverse shear is explicit. The later wrapping/injectivity text on pp.27-29 was inspected for counterevidence. This establishes the sign/strip repair's compatibility, not a new certification of every original global regularity or Minkowski estimate.

problem_reviews.definitions_and_hypotheses: Lemma 2.3 on p.9 assumes an open bounded convex domain. Z=(0,1)^4 and 0<d<1/2 satisfy these assumptions; its erosion is [d,1-d]^4.
problem_reviews.independent_decisive_reason: At x=(d/4,...,d/4), distance to boundary is d/4 but distance to the erosion is 3d/2. Strict inequalities persist on a positive-volume neighborhood. The four-dimensional parallel cube polynomial has terms 8a^3d+6pi a^2d^2+(16pi/3)ad^3+(pi^2/2)d^4; at d=1/4 it differs from 15/16 as reported.
problem_reviews.repair_verified: For rB subset K subset RB after translation, convexity gives (1-d/r)K subset K_d. Support inequalities x.u<=h_K(u)-d<=(1-d/R)h_K(u) give K_d subset (1-d/R)K. Hence (vol K/R)d<=V_d<=(4vol K/r)d. This proves the exact needed order-one premise under unchanged hypotheses.
problem_reviews.counterevidence_and_impact: Open/closed tube conventions do not fix the strict positive-volume discrepancy. The p.22 convex case of Theorem 1.4 uses only the repaired linear decay conclusion; the false intermediate identity remains a local Minor finding.

independent_acceptance.coverage_honesty_review: The report carefully limits all findings to the exact November 2023 arXiv v2 and does not assert journal-version equivalence. Its original execution appendix describes the then-incomplete image gate. The later frozen attachment receipt genuinely completes that unchanged report's physical gate. Current acceptance records distinguish those times and reuse only matching bytes; no current primary full-paper rereview, full ECH rederivation, author-code execution or human review is claimed.
independent_acceptance.decision_explanation: Retain Major for the false exact-exponent quantitative theorem and the invalid displayed symplectic construction, and Minor for the false convex erosion identity whose required conclusion is repaired under unchanged hypotheses. The scalar asymptotics, optimizer exchange, pullback and convex-body inclusions were independently checked. No principal packing or dimension conclusion is refuted. No scientific report revision is necessary. The frozen report's execution appendix is retained as the original initial-stage snapshot; its historical incomplete/EMFILE language is superseded for current delivery only by the separately bound later actual-view/build records and this acceptance, not treated as a current false observation.
